chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Mezzrow's interracial band before Goodman
summary: Freeman recalls Mezz Mezzrow's early-1930s black and white band with Benny Carter and Alex Hill writing, which folded for lack of financing.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Then I got a telegram -- my father got a telegram in Chicago from the Dorsey Brothers again and so I went back to New York from there and then I was never to go back. I went back for short spells with different groups and all that, but then I stayed -- No, I think I went back one more time when Mezzrow was getting a black
and white band together, that was long before Goodman and John Hammond gave the idea to Benny Goodman, as you know.
That's not the one he had in New York.
That was the band that Mezz had in New York, and so we sent for Floyd O'Brien and then we rehearsed --

Yes, remember we played just a few gigs engagements. Too bad that it didn't come off, but it needed financing. It was way ahead of its time because I think Benny was not to -- Lionel and Teddy were not to join Benny Goodman until --
The later thirties and then this band was being organized around '32, wasn't it?
So maybe three or four years later Teddy and Lionel went with Benny.
So Mezzrow was really first in that, I think.
Yes, I think he was, too.
And we had wonderful people like Benny Carter writing for the band, just to help Mezzrow
and doing wonderful things, coming to rehearsal and sitting in and Alex Hill, the great writer-composer-pianist was writing for the band, and he was a marvelous arranger.

And, of course, it was a labor of love sort of thing. I think I played about three or four dates with the band and that was the end of it, and then Joe Venuti came by Mezzrow's apartment and asked me if I would do a record date and work started to open up for me and I left Mezzrow's thing -- of course he had no work to go on and branch out and then I went from one band to another.
